name: Former French Concession
tagline: Plane trees, lane houses and the best cafes in China
description: Straddling Xuhui and Huangpu, the old concession is a grid of narrow streets under London plane trees, lined with 1920s shikumen lane houses and art deco villas. Ground floors hold specialty coffee, natural wine bars and boutiques, and it holds the largest concentration of foreign residents in the city.
bestFor: Nomads who want to walk everywhere and work from a different cafe each day.
pros: Best cafe and restaurant density in Shanghai
Several metro lines cross the area
cons: Most expensive rents in the city
Old lane buildings can be damp with poor heating
Tourist crowds on Wukang Road and Anfu Road

name: Jing'an
tagline: Offices, malls and old lanes in the same block
description: Built around Jing'an Temple and West Nanjing Road, this is the commercial spine of Puxi: glass office towers and luxury malls on the main roads, quiet residential lanes one turn behind them. Coworking spaces are everywhere, and lines 2, 7 and 14 make the rest of the city quick to reach.
bestFor: Nomads who want serviced apartments, coworking desks and airport express links close by.
pros: Dense coworking and serviced apartment supply
Three metro lines through one interchange
Sculpture park and temple grounds for green space
cons: Traffic noise on the main arteries
Less character than the concession streets

name: Changning and Zhongshan Park
tagline: A big park, cheaper rents and a fast line into town
description: West of Jing'an, Changning wraps around Zhongshan Park and the old Hongqiao consular strip. It is a working residential district with wet markets, big malls at the park interchange and plenty of 1990s and 2000s apartment blocks, priced clearly below the concession while staying 15 minutes from it.
bestFor: Longer stays where value per square metre matters more than a Wukang Road address.
pros: Noticeably cheaper than Jing'an or Xuhui
Large park for running and morning exercise
Lines 2, 3 and 4 meet at Zhongshan Park
cons: Older blocks vary a lot in quality
Feels more suburban than central Puxi

name: Hongkou and North Bund
tagline: Old Shanghai streets at the top of the riverfront
description: North of Suzhou Creek, Hongkou holds the old Jewish quarter, Duolun Road's 1920s streetscape and Lu Xun Park, with new riverside towers rising along the North Bund. Rents sit well below the concession, and it remains a lived-in Chinese neighbourhood with morning markets and street food.
bestFor: Nomads who want a local street feel and river walks rather than an expat bubble.
pros: Riverside promenade and large city park
Strong local food scene and markets
cons: Less English spoken day to day
Some blocks are run-down and under redevelopment
Crossing the creek adds time to any trip south

name: Lujiazui, Pudong
tagline: Skyline towers, river views and modern apartments
description: The financial district on the east bank pairs the Shanghai Tower and Jin Mao with newer high-rise residential compounds, gyms and international schools. Everything is newer, cleaner and better maintained than Puxi, and the riverside walk gives you the Bund skyline from the good side of the water.
bestFor: Nomads who want a new, well-equipped apartment and do not mind car-scale streets.
pros: Newest apartment stock with reliable heating and air-con
Fast metro links and closest to Pudong airport
cons: Sterile at street level, built for cars not walkers
Weekend tourist crowds around the towers
Nightlife means crossing back to Puxi
